newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-Chip recovery to aid Dainippon Screen.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Chip recovery to aid Dainippon Screen.

text.p: Japan's Dainippon Screen Manufacturing Co Ltd says that an expected improvement in the global chip market later this year is likely to help its business in the 1998/99 business year and in subsequent years.
Akira Ishida, president of the Kyoto-based manufacturer of precision machinery, told Reuters that he expects the chip market to start recovering this autumn.
"I think the semiconductor market will start recovering this autumn... Demand will boost our earnings in and after the year to March 1999," he said in an interview earlier this week.

For the current fiscal year, however, he said the company's sales may be flat because of uncertainty over the chip market from the demand side. He also said that the firm would like to maintain current profits at last year's level, despite the company's recent forecast of lower profits.

Earlier this month, the company said it expected parent sales of 201 billion yen and current profits of seven billion yen in the current 1997/98 business year. In 1996/97, it posted sales of 200.45 billion yen and current profits of 9.35 billion yen.
Asked whether the company plans to build any new factories for its semiconductor business, Ishida said, "It would be a lie if I said we didn't have such plans."
He added that the company would make a decision when the outlook for future chip demand became clearer.
